title: AI agents rewrite TypeScript compiler in Rust for $24,000
key_facts: Developer and YouTuber Theo Browne used AI agents to port Microsoft's TypeScript compiler, type checker and language server to Rust (project TS_Rust).
He claims the Rust port runs twice as fast as Microsoft's Go-based TypeScript rewrite (v7) and 12.5 times as fast as the previous version (v6), and says he has not inspected the code.
Earlier attempts with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra burned more than $400,000 worth of API-equivalent tokens and reached roughly 84 percent compatibility.

With Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, released last month, he got a working implementation for about $24,000 worth of API-equivalent tokens, passing the conformance tests with nearly 100 percent accuracy.
The model ported Microsoft's Go version to Rust rather than translating from JavaScript, copying a few bugs from the original.
Browne argues a Rust-based TypeScript could let some agent workloads run inside Google's V8 engine instead of VMs or containers, cutting costs.
Microsoft recently rewrote the Copilot runtime in Rust at about $120,000 in AI usage, per The Register.
quote_evidence: With some extra tokens to burn, developer and popular YouTuber Theo Browne used AI agents to port Microsoft's TypeScript compiler to Rust, just to see if it could be done.
The resulting implementation passed the TypeScript conformance tests with nearly 100 percent accuracy.
why_it_matters_hint: AI agents completing a very large code port for tens of thousands of dollars shows how fast the cost of big rewrites is falling, though the claims are one developer's.
notes: Older news re-dated: The Register ran it 15 Oct; Techzine 16 Oct.
